title: Generic basis subtraction and the relative flat locus
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume each fibre ring $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, for $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, is geometrically integral, meaning a nonzero domain after any extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Let $N$ be a finite $A$-module and $\alpha:A^{\oplus r}\to N$ an $A$-linear map with $r\geq0$. For each $\mathfrak p$ let $\xi_{\mathfrak p}\subset A$ be the inverse image of the zero prime of the fibre ring, and assume $N_{\xi_{\mathfrak p}}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\alpha\otimes_A\kappa(\xi_{\mathfrak p})$ is an isomorphism. Set $H=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$. Then $\alpha$ is universally injective over $R$, that is, $L\otimes_R\alpha$ is injective for every $R$-module $L$. For every $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ with inverse image $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the module $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $H_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Finite means finitely generated, and finitely presented means the algebra is a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables modulo finitely many relations; flat means tensoring preserves exact sequences. Localizations and residue fields have their usual meanings [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Fix p∈Spec(R), localize the base to R_p and put A_p=A⊗_R R_p. Flatness and finite presentation localize, and geometric integrality of the fibres is unchanged by this base change. The prime ξ_p becomes the prime mA_p for the maximal ideal m=pR_p, and the hypotheses say that N_{ξ_p} is R_p-flat and that α has an isomorphism on the residue field at mA_p. Apply [lem-trf-local-generic-basis-universal-injective] with q=mA_p. It gives that the localized map α_p:A_p^{⊕r}→N_p is R_p-universally injective (and also that the localized cokernel is flat at ξ_p).

source.place: Tag 05I3, lemma-induction-step, localization to each R_p and implication (1)⇒(2).

proof.text: For any R-module L and base prime p, identify the localization of (A^r tensor_R L → N tensor_R L) at p with (A_p^r tensor_R L → N_p tensor_R L). The source and target identifications use IsLocalizedModule.restrictScalars, IsLocalizedModule.rTensor, and the localization fraction criterion. Tensor cancellation identifies this map with α_p tensor_{R_p} (R_p tensor_R L), which is injective by step 1. The comparisons commute with α on pure tensors. Apply Mathlib injective_of_localized_maximal over R to conclude that α tensor_R L is injective. Tensor symmetry gives the left tensor convention. ULift transports testing modules to a universe containing the modules and recovers exactly the stated testing universe.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, applied after the local 05I3 argument.

proof.text: For any q in Spec A, localize α and the quotient map N → N/range α. Localization preserves exactness and surjectivity. Apply lem-trf-local-universal-injective-localization to the universal injectivity proved above; tensor right exactness makes this localized sequence universally short exact. If N_q is R-flat, lem-trf-local-ui-flat-cokernel gives R-flatness of the localized quotient. For the converse, the localized source (A^r)_q is flat over A_q, hence over A and R by transitivity. Universal injectivity, tested at R (using ULift), implies injectivity of the localized α. The already proved source-library theorem Module.Flat.of_exact_of_flat_of_flat then says that the extension of the flat quotient by this flat source is flat. Thus N_q is R-flat if and only if the localized quotient is R-flat; these are equivalent to the R_p-flatness formulations by Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization.

lean.statement: theorem free_subtraction_flatness (R A : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Module.Flat R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] [GeometricallyIntegral (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))] (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R A N] [Module.Finite A N] (r : ℕ) (α : (Fin r → A) →ₗ[A] N) (ξ : PrimeSpectrum R → PrimeSpectrum A) (hξ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, (ξ p).asIdeal = RingHom.ker (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : A →ₐ[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A)) (hgenericFlat : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule (ξ p).asIdeal.primeCompl N)) (hgenericBasis : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Function.Bijective (α.baseChange (ξ p).asIdeal.ResidueField)) : (∀ (L : Type (max u w)) [AddCommGroup L] [Module R L], Function.Injective ((α.restrictScalars R).lTensor L)) ∧ ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum A, Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl N) ↔ Module.Flat R (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range α))
lean.note: The generic primes ξ are specified uniquely by the kernels of the canonical maps into the fibre rings. Flatness of each localized module is expressed over R, equivalently over R_p for its canonical localized-base action, by Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization; no hypothesis or conclusion is changed.
